helpful: The statpack merits section's per-Term table with the excluded count made the pooled baseline a two-minute computation with no judgment calls.
documents.json's empty_text marker made the BIO's unavailability unambiguous — content-unavailable rather than absent.
gaps: No way to hydrate a provisioned document that was fetched but had no text layer (the BIO here) — an OCR pass at provisioning time would have closed my largest evidentiary gap.

fedcourts query has no free-text or subject filter, and its citation filter is own-cites only, so there is no corpus route to 'SCOTUS merits outcomes in immigration statutory-interpretation cases' — the cut a merits cell most wants; one unproductive citation lookup cost ~348 MB of ranged reads.

No committed cut of merits outcomes conditioned on split shape (grant from the majority vs minority side of a circuit split), which is the main case-specific adjustment a grant-moment merits cell makes from the pooled rate.
notes: Forward merits cell at the grant moment: the record was current to today and the merits briefs do not exist yet, so retrieval had little to add beyond the provisioned petition and the committed statpack.
